title: New-window links and scripted popups are silently discarded
impact: Ordinary website links that request another tab do nothing. Popup-based authentication cannot complete through this handler.
recommendation: Separate external website navigation policy from sealed visualization policy. Dispatch ordinary new-tab requests through the service and explicitly support or explain authentication popups.
acceptance: In one local fixture, same-tab navigation, target=_blank, middle-click, and a scripted popup each produce the documented destination or a visible actionable refusal. The opener-based fixture can report a successful callback.

title: Website JavaScript dialogs are always dismissed
impact: An action gated by confirm cannot receive affirmative consent; prompt cannot collect input, and alert messages never reach the operator.
recommendation: Keep sealed visualization restrictions, but supply a native or GPUI dialog bridge for external pages, with a deliberate suppression state when appropriate.
acceptance: A local confirm fixture executes its positive branch after the user chooses OK; Cancel returns false. Prompt returns entered text, and alert is visible. No website can replace the app window.

title: Right-click has no browser context menu
impact: Operators cannot discover normal link, image, selection, and editable-field actions through right-click.
recommendation: Introduce a browser-specific context menu using native hit-test details. Do not apply arbitrary website menus to sealed content.
acceptance: Right-click a link and copy its destination; right-click selected page text and copy it; paste into an input through the menu. Each action operates on the clicked page.

title: Browser tabs discard page titles and show only hostnames
impact: Two pages on the same host, including two localhost apps on different ports, have indistinguishable tab labels. Favicons are absent.
recommendation: Carry page identity metadata through service state and render title, favicon, and a full-address tooltip. Keep port in the fallback.
acceptance: Tabs titled Docs and Dashboard on one origin remain distinguishable; two untitled localhost ports show distinct fallback labels. Title changes update the correct tab.

title: Address entry rejects normal schemeless hostnames
impact: Common development addresses such as localhost:3000 require manual http:// entry.
recommendation: Normalize human address input separately from the service authorization policy. Do not weaken scheme restrictions or silently turn arbitrary text into a network destination.
acceptance: localhost:3000 opens http://localhost:3000; example.com opens https://example.com. Explicit unsupported schemes still produce clear errors.

title: Page navigation can overwrite an unfinished address edit
impact: A redirect or same-page URL change can replace the address the user is currently typing.
recommendation: Introduce explicit address editing state. Show committed URL while idle; preserve and validate the draft while editing; Escape should restore the committed URL.
acceptance: Type a new URL during a delayed redirect and a history.pushState update. The draft survives both. Escape restores the final page URL, and Enter navigates to the draft.

title: New-tab mode leaves navigation controls pointed at the hidden old page
impact: Clicking Reload or Back while an empty new tab is shown unexpectedly acts on the previous tab and abandons new-tab entry.
recommendation: Model the displayed target explicitly or consistently derive toolbar state from the displayed page. Keep draft new-tab state independent of the previous document.
acceptance: After clicking plus, Back, Forward, and Reload cannot affect the old page. The address draft remains until explicit submission, cancel, or tab selection.

title: Loading changes browser geometry and shifts the address field
impact: Loading moves the page and changes its actual viewport size. The Annotate button also appears and disappears, changing address width.
recommendation: Reserve one compact navigation row; keep annotation visible but disabled during loading and place progress in an overlay or fixed-height track.
acceptance: Record the page origin, page viewport size, and address bounds before and during a slow navigation. All remain stable, and loading remains visible. Narrow-width controls stay operable.

title: Viewport size is inseparable from panel size
impact: The operator cannot verify a site at a precise mobile or desktop viewport, rotate a preset, or compare a large layout while keeping the chat readable.
recommendation: Add a user-selected viewport mode distinct from host size and device pixel ratio, plus explicit page zoom. Validate dimensions and preserve selection per browser tab.
acceptance: A 390 by 844 preset reports those CSS dimensions in the page while the right panel is resized; rotate swaps dimensions; Fill restores host-sized layout. Zoom has a visible reset.

title: Find, DevTools, hard reload, and page appearance controls are absent
impact: Long-page search and normal web development inspection require leaving the embedded browser. Cache bypass and theme checks have no operator controls.
recommendation: Add typed page operations and a browser menu. Keep find scoped to the website rather than transcript search; surface supported runtime distinctions.
acceptance: Find highlights matches and cycles next/previous in the current page; DevTools targets the correct tab; hard reload bypasses a fixture cache; light/dark setting updates a media-query fixture.

title: Inactive-page reclamation restores only a URL, losing navigation and page position
impact: A clean tab can lose its Back/Forward stack, scroll position, and transient UI state merely because it was hidden. Restart also restores only URLs and selection.
recommendation: Preserve native tabs for normal switching or retain a navigation/session snapshot before reclaiming. Define the resource policy explicitly instead of immediate hidden-state disposal. Do not claim full T3 session restoration without checking its host lifetime.
acceptance: Visit A then B, scroll B, switch away and back through actual reclamation, and verify Back returns to A and B restores its scroll. Repeat after restart according to the documented persistence contract.

title: An empty browser provides neither useful guidance nor recent/local destinations
impact: Opening the browser or a new tab leaves the user to recover a URL manually from terminal output or memory.
recommendation: Render an actual empty/new-tab page with address guidance, scoped recent destinations, and discovered local servers. Reuse existing terminal/server discovery if available rather than introducing another scanner.
acceptance: First open and last-tab close show guidance. Starting a local development server yields a clearly labeled destination, and a recently visited URL can be reopened and removed.

title: Persistent website profiles have no operator management controls
impact: Cookies survive sessions, but the operator cannot clear broken authentication/cache or choose isolated browser identities from the browser UI.
recommendation: First add visible active-profile identity and scoped clear-cookie/cache operations. Treat multi-profile, private sessions, and cookie import as separate product choices; do not import credentials without an explicit user action.
acceptance: A fixture cookie persists normally, clears through the named profile action, and stays isolated from another chosen profile if multi-profile support is adopted. The UI states which data will be cleared.

title: Browser capture is annotation-oriented and lacks direct recording/export affordances
impact: An operator cannot directly record a browser interaction or capture a plain screenshot through the browser chrome for external sharing.
recommendation: Reuse the existing capture pipeline for a plain screenshot command with output feedback. Decide recording scope separately; show active recording and its destination rather than hiding it behind a modifier-only gesture.
acceptance: A direct screenshot contains the current page at the chosen scale and can be opened from the reported destination. If recording is added, start/stop yields a playable file with a visible active-state indicator.

title: Errors occupy an inline text row with repetitive recovery copy
impact: Failure details compete with the page and can wrap through much of a narrow panel. The recovery action is described in text rather than placed beside the message.
recommendation: Classify load, HTTP, engine, and profile errors. Give each a short summary and relevant action, with details behind disclosure. Keep layout stable and decide whether the failed page is meaningfully annotatable.
acceptance: Offline, refused connection, HTTP error, and unavailable engine each show one concise explanation and the correct retry/repair action at narrow panel widths, without repeated recovery sentences.

title: No browser-chrome escape to the system browser
impact: When a website needs unsupported authentication, downloads, permissions, or development tools, the operator must manually copy the address and leave the app.
recommendation: Add Open in system browser for the committed page URL, with an error if launching fails. Do not send the unsubmitted address draft.
acceptance: The action opens the current page in the configured browser; an unfinished address draft does not change the launched destination.
